name: get_engine_info
description: Returns the engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status. Call it first, to check that the engine is new enough and to see which toolchain packages are downloaded. It is fast and local: it never uses the network. Missing packages are downloaded automatically by the tools that need them, unless auto_download is off.

name: download_packages
description: Downloads or repairs the engine's toolchain packages from the internet, into its engine folder. Packages that are already ready are left alone, unless force is set to download them again. Other tools download the packages they need on their own, so call this only to download ahead of time, such as before going offline, or when a tool returns a setup error with the download_packages action (for example when the engine was launched with automatic download turned off). A download can take a few minutes; the tool reports progress and can be cancelled.

force.description:
Download the packages again even if they are ready, replacing the
current copies. Use it when a package's tools fail in
ways that suggest damaged files. Defaults to false. Don't use it while
other operations are running.

name: check_updates
description: Checks now for newer releases of the engine's packages (the board catalog and the FPGA tools): reads the engine's remote config, downloads what it names that isn't downloaded yet, and uses it from the next call. name: get_catalog
description: Returns board and FPGA definitions from the engine's read-only catalog. Use it to find a board's catalog ID, such as icesugar-1-5, to pass as the board of other tools, or to see a board's FPGA and how it is programmed. Each section is returned only when asked for: {"boards": {"fetch": true}} returns all boards, and {"boards": {"fetch": true, "ids": ["icesugar-1-5"]}} only the listed ones. Boards include those of the request's custom_boards_folder, marked custom, a custom board replacing the catalog board with its ID. The families section gives each FPGA family's name for people, the extension of its pin constraint files and the toolchain that builds it. Board descriptions are the boards' names for people.

boards.description: Which boards to return. Omitted means none.

fpgas.description: Which FPGAs to return. Omitted means none.

families.description:
Which FPGA families to return, by ID, such as ice40 or gw1n.
Omitted means none.

custom_boards_folder.description:
The host's own boards: the absolute path of a folder of board files,
one board each in the catalog's format, named by board ID, such as
boards/my-board.json (a project's boards folder). board can name one
of them; one with a catalog board's ID replaces that board in this
request. Problems in any file come back as a request error with a
diagnostic for each, at file, line and column. Send the same folder to
every tool. Omitted means none.

display_paths.description:
How to name paths in what people read (diagnostics, messages,
testbench output, live tool output, diagram labels): files named as
a whole, then folders whose files keep their path below the folder
under the folder's new name ("" gives names relative to it); the
first match in each list wins. Paths are compared by real location.
Never applied to command lines or fields that are paths. Omitted
means paths read as the request gave them.

CatalogQuery.description: Selects entries from one catalog section.

fetch.description: Whether to return this section. Defaults to false.

ids.description:
Catalog IDs of the entries to return. Omitted means all entries. An
ID that isn't in the section is an error.

How to name paths in what people read: diagnostics, messages, testbench

files.description:

folders.description:

path.description: The file or folder, as an absolute path.

The standard dimensions, connection then memory, each with the values

requires.description:
What every design for the board must do, such as driving a pin

must do. Omitted when nothing.

resources.description:
What the board wires to FPGA pins, by port name, each of a type with
its own fields: clock (pin, mhz), leds, buttons and switches (pins,
active), rgb_led (red, green, blue, active), led_matrix (leds,
colors, active), uart (tx, rx), pmod (its 8 signal pins), header,
and unclassified (every wired pin no other resource lists). A name
with one pin is a plain port, with several a vector, bit 0 first.
The order of resources means nothing. A resource's requires lists
what must be done for it to work, such as a jumper a clock needs (a
setup). For creating designs and pin files for the board, such as a
blinky. Omitted when none are known; a type a board doesn't list is unknown,
unless the board has an unclassified resource.

family.description:

nextpnr_device.description:
The device nextpnr uses, such as hx8k for iCE40, 25k for ECP5,
GW1NR-LV9QN88PC6/I5 for Gowin or xc7a35tcsg324-1 for Xilinx.

nextpnr_package.description:
The package nextpnr uses, such as tq144:4k for iCE40 or CABGA256 for
ECP5. Required for iCE40 and ECP5; Gowin and Xilinx have none,
since their nextpnr_device names the package.

The speed grade nextpnr uses, such as 6. ECP5 only, where it's
required.

nextpnr_family.description:
The device family nextpnr uses, such as GW1N-9C, when nextpnr can't
tell it from nextpnr_device. Gowin only, optional.

packer_device.description:
The device the bitstream packer (gowin_pack) uses, such as GW1N-9C.
Gowin only, where it's required.

jtag_idcode.description:
The FPGA's JTAG ID code, such as 0x0362d093, as openFPGALoader's
--detect reports it. Before programming over JTAG, the engine reads
the connected FPGA's ID code and refuses to program a different
FPGA, such as a board of another size than the build's. It
identifies the chip, not the size a board uses it as, so FPGAs made
from the same chip share it. ECP5, Gowin and Xilinx only, optional:
without it there is no check.

family's FPGAs are in the catalog's `fpgas/<family>.json`.

name: diagram
description: Draws the design as schematic diagrams, one per module: registers, adders, comparators, multiplexers, memories, the FPGA's own blocks and other modules as symbols, with the wires between them. Yosys reads the design as written, without synthesizing it, and the engine lays out and draws every module itself. Writes, in the build folder's diagram/ folder (replaced by each call): diagram.html, one self-contained page with every module (click a module to open it, drag to pan, scroll to zoom, hover anything for its details; it needs no network or other software, so any web browser shows it), each module's SVG, and diagram.json, a model of every module's blocks, ports, signals and source lines. To show the user the diagram, set open to true, which opens the page in their web browser, or give them page_file's path. List the design files; the engine doesn't search for them. Errors in the design, such as a syntax error or a top module that isn't in the files, are design errors with diagnostics at file and line. The first call may download the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes.

name: build
description: Builds an FPGA design into a bitstream: synthesizes the Verilog or SystemVerilog sources, places and routes them on the board's FPGA using the constraint file, which maps top-level ports to pins (.pcf for iCE40, .lpf for ECP5, .cst for Gowin, .xdc for Xilinx), and packs the bitstream into the build folder. Give the source files explicitly; the engine doesn't search for them, though `include files are found next to the including file or in the source folder. A build with no changes since the last one returns at once with up_to_date set. The first build may download the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. Design problems come back as a design error with diagnostics at file and line. After a successful build, program_board programs the bitstream into the board.

description: Deletes build folders. Given a build folder, such as /home/user/proj/_build, it deletes it. Given a folder of build folders, such as /home/user/proj/builds with one build folder per board, it deletes each build folder directly inside it, then the folder itself if nothing else is left. Given a build_folder, it lists only the devices that fit that build's board and variant, best first, each with its build_match: program the only one, or ask the user when there are several. Devices that need a driver or permissions first are listed apart, under unreachable, with the fix. On Windows, a device whose board's programmer needs a driver has driver: the one it needs (WinUSB), on which USB interface, the one it has and whether it's ready.

name: program_board
description: Programs the bitstream of a successful build into the board it was built for. It doesn't build: call build first, and program_board only if the build succeeded. The board comes from the build, so it takes the build folder and the device to program: the id of a device from list_devices whose boards include the build's board (ask the user when several do). A device that isn't connected anymore is a setup error with connect_board; list the devices again. On ECP5, Gowin and Xilinx boards it first reads the connected FPGA's ID code and refuses a different FPGA, such as a board of another size than the build's, before writing anything. Most boards are programmed to flash, so the design stays after power-off.

diagnostic for each, at file, line and column. Send the same folder to
every tool. Omitted means none.

display_paths.description:
How to name paths in what people read (diagnostics, messages,
testbench output, live tool output, diagram labels): files named as
a whole, then folders whose files keep their path below the folder
under the folder's new name ("" gives names relative to it); the
first match in each list wins. Paths are compared by real location.
Never applied to command lines or fields that are paths. Omitted
means paths read as the request gave them.

DisplayPaths.description:
How to name paths in what people read: diagnostics, messages, testbench
output, live tool output and diagram labels. Never command lines or
fields that are paths.

files.description:
Files named as a whole. They come before folders; the first that
matches wins.

folders.description:
Folders whose files keep their path below the folder, under the
folder's name `as`. The first that matches wins.

DisplayPath.description: One file or folder and how to name it.

path.description: The file or folder, as an absolute path.

as.description:
How people read it: any text. For a folder, a path inside it keeps
its part below the folder after this and "/", or alone when this is
empty, so "" gives names relative to the folder.

programmer.description:
The programmer that was used, such as openfpgaloader, or custom for a
programmer_command.

commands.description:
The programs this call ran, in order, each with the exact command and
a shell line that runs it again without the engine, such as for a bug
report to the tool's developers.

Device.description: A connected device that the engine can open.

id.description:
The device's ID, to pass to program_board. Opaque: don't parse it.
It names the device on this computer for a short time: it stays
valid while the device stays on the same USB port, so list the
devices again before asking the user to choose.

label.description:
The device for people: its product name (else its manufacturer's
name, else "USB device"), then its manufacturer and USB IDs, such
as "Alhambra II v1.0A (AlhambraBits, 0403:6010)".

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits.

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name the device reports, when available.

product.description: The product name the device reports, when available.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports, when available.

device.description:
USB device number on its bus. It changes when the device is plugged
in again.

boards.description:
The boards whose USB filters this device matches, best first. Empty
for a device that is no known board.

likely_boards.description:
The boards this device most likely is, best first: those of boards
at its strongest match level, unless that is weak (many boards fit,
so none is likely). Empty when no board is likely.

build_match.description:
How well the device matches the given build's board in the build's
variant: strong, possible or weak, as in boards. Present only when
list_devices was given a build_folder.

driver.description:
On Windows only: the driver the device needs for its board's
programmer (the build's board when list_devices was given a
build_folder, else its best match) and the one it has, for a board
whose programmer needs one. ready false means install_driver first.

oneOf.description: A USB device.

BoardMatch.description: A board a device may be.

board.description:
The board's ID: a catalog ID, or a custom board's ID when custom is
true.

custom.description:
True when the board is from the request's custom boards folder rather
than the catalog's.

variants.description:
The board's variants this device fits, in the board's order, each
with its own match level. Use the level of the variant you mean,
such as the build's.

VariantMatch.description: A variant of a board that a device fits.

selector.description:
The variant's selector, such as {"connection": "usb", "memory":
"flash"}, as board_variant gives it in requests.

match.description:
How well the device matches the board in this variant: strong,
possible or weak. See MatchLevel.

Selector.description:
Which of a board's variants: a value of each standard dimension. In a
board definition it says where the variant sits; in requests
(board_variant) it picks the variant with these values.

connection.description:
How the computer reaches the board: usb, bootloader, ft2232h,
ft232h, cmsis-dap, usb-blaster or unspecified (see the dimensions).

memory.description:
Where the design goes: flash (kept at power-off) or ram (lost at
power-off).

MatchLevel.description:
How well a device matches a board, by what it means for the user, not
by its cause. The criteria are internal to the engine and change
without notice, so hosts must not infer why a device matched; they may
only show the level and compare levels (weak < possible < strong). No
level proves which board is connected.

oneOf.description: The device fits the board, but so do many other boards.

The device could be the board, but a few other boards look the
same.
The device is very likely the board.

DriverStatus.description:
The driver a device needs for a board's programmer on Windows, and the
one it has: in list_devices, on Windows only, for devices whose board
needs one.

needed.description: The driver the board's programmer needs: winusb.

interface.description:
The USB interface that needs it, such as 0 (an FTDI chip's first
channel; its other channels, such as a serial port, keep their
driver).

current.description:
The driver Windows has on that interface now, by its service name in
lowercase, such as ftdibus (FTDI's), usbser or winusb. Omitted when
it has none.

ready.description:
Whether the programmer can use the interface as it is: true with
WinUSB, and with libusbK or libusb0, which older guides installed.
False means install_driver (WinUSB) first.

CommandRecord.description: One program the engine ran, with what it takes to run it again.

tool.description: The program's name, such as yosys.

package.description:
The package the program came from, with its version and the core's
tool, such as "logix-core 2026.11.10 (oss-cad-suite)". Omitted for a
program from elsewhere, such as a custom programmer command.

cwd.description: The folder it ran in, as an absolute path.

args.description:
The program as an absolute path, then its arguments, exactly as
passed.

shell.description:
One shell command line that runs it again the same way: in the same
folder, with the same minimal environment (PATH, the home and
temporary folders and, on Windows, the variables its programs need).
